messages:
raj: Quick legal question about onboarding a new community model (Orion-7B). License includes an "Attribution" clause that says 'prominent attribution with model name + source link required in public-facing products'. We're planning: (1) serve via Hosted API, (2) run int4 quant experiments and host quantized runtimes in Dedicated, (3) publish benchmark results and a short eval writeup. Does the attribution requirement apply to the runtime responses (i.e. the UI), the docs only, or both? Also, is storing/serving quantized weights considered redistribution?
tara: Short version: if the model's outputs are exposed to end users in a public-facing product, attribution must be reasonably prominent where users see the output. Docs alone (e.g., a deep-dive legal page) often won't cut it for interactive products. For Hosted API customers we should provide a standard attribution snippet they can paste into their UI or docs.

On quantization: creating a quantized artifact is a derivative work in many licenses. "Distributing" those derived weights (e.g., uploading them to a repo, sharing with third parties) counts as redistribution and triggers any redistribution restrictions. Running the weights only on our servers to serve responses typically does not constitute redistribution, but check for explicit "hosting" or "service" prohibitions in the license text. If the license forbids commercial hosting, that's a blocker for our Hosted offering without a license exception.

devin: Re: benchmarks — we publish prompts + outputs on a public leaderboard page. Is that considered "public-facing" for attribution? We also sometimes release anonymized sample outputs in blog posts.
tara: Yes, the leaderboard & blog posts are public-facing and should include the attribution snippet. For outputs we recommend including a short line under examples: "Model: Orion-7B (source link)." Also be careful not to publish or attach model weights or full parameter dumps. If you share evaluation artifacts with partners/contractors, use an NDA or a DPA and record that sharing in the model onboarding ticket.

maria: Suggestion for operational changes: add three onboarding fields on the model entry form — attribution_snippet (short text we can show in UI), redistribute_allowed (yes/no), hosting_allowed (yes/no or restricted). Also add a checkbox: 'quantized artifacts may NOT be publicly redistributed'. We can auto-generate the model-card with the attribution snippet and license link.

raj: Good. One edge: enterprise customers sometimes want to remove attribution branding in their product. If they call our Hosted API and surface outputs in their private app, are we responsible for enforcing attribution downstream?
tara: If the customer is the one embedding model outputs in their product, the obligation generally flows to them. However, if the license forbids removal of attribution for downstream users, we should disallow provisioning the model to customers that will strip attribution (or require contractual terms). For enterprise deals, add a line in the contract requiring the customer to preserve attribution for any public-facing surfaces. Escalate to Legal for any carve-outs.

devin: One more: we want to run cross-model quantized benchmarks and share relative latency/cost numbers (no weights). Any red flags?
tara: That's fine. Include the attribution snippet on the benchmark page, and be explicit about testing methodology and PT/INT formats used. Do not publish quantized weight files. If you want to share a container image for reproducibility, ensure it does not embed the weights or that you have redistribution rights.

legal-bot: Ticket INF-842 created to add onboarding flags (attribution_snippet, redistribute_allowed, hosting_allowed) and to track a legal review for Orion-7B. Assigned to @tara and @maria.

maria: I'll add the onboarding fields and a model-card template example. Will link to INF-842 and ping team when ready.

raj: Thanks — will hold off on any weight-sharing and will include the attribution snippet on the public benchmark page once it's available.
